edits.name: Paired-device command deny list before any Mac or phone is paired (computer.act, Mac host commands, iPhone data commands), plus the off switches
edits.description: Make 'no agent can drive, run commands on or view any Mac, or pull data from a paired phone' an explicit Gateway setting instead of a side effect of no app being installed, and write down the three ways to switch computer control off. Nothing is paired today, so the family sees no change; it is the gate the iPhone app (OCL-01) and the screen-control pilot (MAC-02) must pass first.
edits.how: Add `computer.act` to `gateway.nodes.commands.deny` in happy-config, and while no Mac node is wanted also every desktop host command the docs list as arriving with a Mac pairing: `system.run`, `system.run.prepare`, `system.which`, `browser.proxy`, `browser.proxy.upload.v1`, `mcp.tools.call.v1`, `screen.snapshot` and `desktop.stream`. A deny entry always wins over platform defaults and allow entries, matches exact command names, withholds the command (for `computer.act`, together with the node's `computer` capability) and is logged. The list is Gateway-wide, so the same change carries the phone ceiling for the iPhone app entry (OCL-01): deny the iOS default data commands (`location.get`, `contacts.search`, `calendar.events`, `reminders.list`, `photos.latest`, `motion.activity`, `motion.pedometer`), keep the opt-in commands (`camera.snap`, `camera.clip`, `screen.record`, `health.summary`, `contacts.add`, `calendar.add`, `reminders.add`) out of `gateway.nodes.commands.allow`, and set `gateway.nodes.pluginTools.enabled: false` so a paired device cannot publish tools to agents. Keep `computer` absent from every agent's tool lists; the per-person agents already deny `group:nodes`, which contains it, and the inbox agent denies every tool. Set `gateway.nodes.pairing.sshVerify: false` (SSH-verified pairing is on by default) and do not use setup links for a Mac, since either can approve a node's first command surface automatically. The deny list covers paired nodes; control of the Gateway's own desktop is a separate route that the docs say needs the `cua-computer` plugin explicitly enabled on the Gateway host, so leave that plugin not enabled on the Mac mini. For reference, the documented gate stack for screen control is: tool policy exposes `computer` to an agent; gateway command policy; device pairing and then a second, distinct approval of the node's command surface; the switch inside the Mac app; and the macOS permissions. Exec approvals gate shell commands on a node, not clicks. Off switches during a pilot: (1) put the deny line back (command-policy changes reach connected nodes under the default hybrid reload, with no restart); (2) the G005 kill file checked in the desk hook; (3) on the Mac, turn off 'Allow Computer Control' (rechecked at each invocation) or revoke Accessibility.

caveats: The guest is not empty of secrets: OpenClaw.app inside it is signed in to the family gateway, so until the app is shown to run as a node with no operator rights, the agent driving the screen can open a console to everything the clean desk was built to keep away.

The gateway is bound to loopback and published only through Tailscale Serve, so the guest needs an SSH tunnel, its own tailnet identity or a wider gateway bind, and each of those changes the M0 baseline and needs its own review.
Pairing the Mac app pairs a whole node: shell execution, a browser proxy, node MCP calls and a desktop stream arrive together with pointer control.
A hook sees typed parameters and not meaning, so an action allowlist cannot stop the model clicking the wrong thing, and what exists on the controlled desktop is the real boundary.
The approval on the first action only proves that a parent started the task: the dozens of clicks after it run unreviewed, and the prompt is text only with no screenshot.
Red-team research on computer-use agents reports injected on-screen instructions succeeding in a large share of attempts, so the tool's built-in warning to the model is a tripwire and not a control.
A desktop that is never reset is the agent's memory, because files, open windows and the clipboard carry over from one run, or one parent, to the next.

Whether Computer Control works inside a macOS guest with a virtual display, and whether an approval raised inside a spawned desk run reaches the asking parent's chat, are both untested, and a pass on the acceptance test shows usefulness, not safety.

In OpenClaw 2026.9.7 the `computer` tool can also target the Gateway's own desktop once the `cua-computer` plugin is enabled on the Gateway host. Leave that plugin not enabled on the Mac mini and have the hook require the guest's node id on every call, so a run can never land on happy's desktop.

edits.how:
1. Ceiling first, before any phone is paired: confirm the wave-A deny list (MAC-04) is deployed. It denies the iOS default data commands, keeps the opt-in commands (camera, screen recording, Health and the contact, calendar and reminder writes) out of gateway.nodes.commands.allow and sets gateway.nodes.pluginTools.enabled: false, so a paired phone cannot publish tools to agents. The deny list matches exact command names, so unless Talk (VOX-01) is being set up also list talk.ptt.start, talk.ptt.stop, talk.ptt.cancel and talk.ptt.once. 2. Install the App Store app on Tony's iPhone and pair it with a setup code from the Control UI (Nodes, Devices, Pair device) or openclaw qr over the existing Tailscale Serve URL. One code issues a node session and an operator session together; an administrator-minted code approves the device and its first declared command surface in one step, so read the approved command list afterwards and approve any later widening by hand. 3. Access level: Full access carries operator.admin, which is what lets the app review pending exec approvals in general; Limited access drops only operator.admin (write, read and approvals scopes remain) and the docs then promise approval review only for requests that explicitly target that device. 4. Agents: do not grant the built-in nodes tool to any agent (it is owner-only, on the sandbox default deny list, and carries approve and raw invoke actions); if a later feature needs one phone command, use a small in-house plugin tool over api.runtime.nodes.invoke with the node id and command fixed in code. Deny show_widget on

-main, or allow native reports only. 5. Uploads from the app go through the F084 privacy gate, or are switched off with gateway.uploads.enabled: false. iMessage stays the main channel; the app is the surface for long documents, tap approvals and a fallback if imsg breaks after a macOS update. Out of scope for this entry: a second adult's phone. Every setup code carries Gateway-wide operator scopes, OpenClaw says those are not isolation between people, and roadmap section 1b keeps the control plane with Tony while family members only chat. Reopening that is Tony's decision, and it would first need named operator roles (gateway.roles) bound to a verified identity and rehearsed on a test profile, because a Gateway with roles configured refuses operator connections that carry only a device or setup-code token.

caveats: Pairing defaults to Full access (operator.admin): the app then also opens Dashboard settings, automations and every agent. Limited access drops only operator.admin; it keeps operator.write, operator.read and operator.approvals, which the docs describe as Gateway-wide, so a Limited phone can still run any agent. Only a role bound to a verified identity narrows that.

With gateway.roles configured, operator connections that authenticate only with device or bootstrap tokens are refused; whether the iPhone app can present a per-person verified identity instead is not confirmed (see unverified).
App Store builds receive push through OpenClaw's hosted relay, a service outside the tailnet; the Gateway stores a relay handle rather than the raw APNs token.
iOS suspends the app in the background: camera and screen node commands need the app in front, and voice is best-effort.
Files a parent uploaded earlier cannot yet be downloaded again from native history; assistant-sent documents are capped at 100 MB.
Progress cards and inline widgets only exist on app and web surfaces, so behaviour will differ between the app and the iMessage thread.
iMessage already covers quick text, and with attachment intake (F002) it also takes photos and PDFs; the app earns its place only for long multi-page documents, tap approvals and offline queueing.

Turning on gateway.roles changes sign-in for every operator device: connections that authenticate only with device or bootstrap tokens are refused, including a setup-code iPhone and any of Tony's existing token-paired devices. The docs also say roles organise collaboration inside one trust domain and are not a per-person isolation boundary. Rehearse on a test profile before touching the live Gateway.
